requirement_title: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true
requirement_text:
# REQ-2234: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2234
Type: bug

## Requirement

The analyzer does not work if `SuppressSourceGeneration = true`. This has happened since version 3.1.1. It still worked in 3.1.0.

(The upstream issue contains no further text, repro or comments. Anything beyond this is derived.)

## Acceptance criteria

- With `SuppressSourceGeneration = true`, the MessagePack analyzer still reports its diagnostics (MsgPack0xx rules) for code that violates them. (derived)
- Behaviour with `SuppressSourceGeneration = true` matches version 3.1.0, where the analyzer worked. (derived)
- Behaviour with `SuppressSourceGeneration` unset or false does not change. (derived)
- Source generation itself stays suppressed when `SuppressSourceGeneration = true`. (derived)

## Notes from discussion

No comments on the issue.

findings.claim: The duplicate-key guard for inherited string-keyed members has no covering test. The added duplicate-string-key case declares both members on the same class and therefore does not exercise a collision between base and derived members.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:1176 remove-guard: if (!stringMembers.ContainsKey(member.StringKey)) -> unconditional stringMembers.Add(member.StringKey, (member, item.Type)); expected to survive because no added test uses duplicate string keys across an inheritance hierarchy.

no test in the suite detects delete-statement at src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:1178

hunches.claim: The new `continue` changes generator behavior even when `SuppressSourceGeneration` is false: after reporting the mixed-key diagnostic, a mismatched-key member is no longer added to the collected member maps or processed for formatter metadata. Consequently, checked-in/generated formatter output for such types changes, although the requirement limits the fix to making analysis work while generation is suppressed and explicitly requires unchanged behavior when suppression is false.

receipt_plan.detail: Run generator snapshot tests with base and head for a source-generated [MessagePackObject] containing one [Key(0)] member and one [Key("name")] member, with SuppressSourceGeneration=false. Verify MsgPack006 is reported in both builds and compare generated formatter source; the head build skips the string-keyed member after the new continue. Repeat for the string-key-first loop with an int-keyed mismatch.

hunches.claim: MsgPack017 is incorrectly classified as source-generation-only. Its warning about an init property initializer being discarded also applies when the suppressed type is serialized through the dynamic resolver, so omitting it loses a relevant runtime diagnostic and changes the documented suppressed-type behavior.

receipt_plan.detail: Add an analyzer test for [MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)] containing a keyed init property with a non-default initializer, marked with an expected MsgPack017 diagnostic. The test should fail with the changed suppression behavior; ledger [L6] describes the diagnostic as a deserialization behavior, not a formatter-generation-only check.

hunches.claim: The new continue in the inherited-member collection path is not exercised: every added analyzer test uses a single flat class, so none mixes key kinds between a derived type and its serializable base type.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:1148 delete-statement: continue; -> removed; expected to survive because no added test has an inherited [MessagePackObject] member whose key kind differs from the other members.
